{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Charter schools were originally intended to be publicly funded schools with increased flexibility in program design and operations.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Democrats believe education is a public good and should not be saddled with a private profit motive.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for banning for-profit private charter businesses from receiving federal funding.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Recognition of the need for more stringent guardrails to ensure charter schools are good stewards of federal education funds.",
"claim_types":["characterization"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for measures to increase accountability for charter schools, including by requiring all charter schools to meet the same standards of transparency as traditional public schools, including with regard to civil rights protections, racial equity, admissions practices, disciplinary procedures, and school finances.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Support for conditioning federal funding for new, expanded charter schools or for charter school renewals on a district's review of whether the charter will systematically underserve the neediest students.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Opposition to private school vouchers and other policies that divert taxpayer-funded resources away from the public school system, including the program at issue in the recent Espinoza decision.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
